title: Reviewing the paperwork burden on court-appointed deputies under the Mental Capacity Act
asked: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng asked whether the Ministry for Social and Family Development will review the administrative and reporting framework for court-appointed deputies under the Mental Capacity Act, to simplify procedures and ease the compliance burden while keeping safeguards for the people they serve.
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming said court-appointed deputies must file an annual report with the Office of the Public Guardian, a safeguard requiring them to set out how they discharged their Court-ordered responsibilities, including decisions made for the person and management of their property and affairs. He said MSF has worked to reduce the burden through online report submission, a built-in finance tracker, monthly OPG workshops and personalised filing support. On the supplementary question, he said a deputy's responsibilities are broader than under an LPA and vary with what the Court decides, and that MSF will continuously review the application and reporting processes and the overall deputyship experience. He also said MSF notes Mr Patrick Tay's suggestion on thresholds and will take a look at it.

key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: it requires deputies to set out how they have discharged their responsibilities under the Court order

key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: We will take a look at it.

left_open: Whether an inter-agency work group, including volunteers, will be set up to coordinate help for family-member deputies and make information available to them
How the inconsistent support from banks for these families will be addressed
Whether any threshold or alternative to full deputyship, such as a statutory declaration, will be introduced
supplementary: Difficulties applying for and complying with deputyship, banking constraints, and whether thresholds or an inter-agency work group could ease the burden.
